content: To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all.
author: Oscar Wilde
sourceWork: The Soul of Man under Socialism (1891)
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

In Oscar Wilde's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: Are your days primarily filled with existing and reacting to demands, or are you carving out intentional space for the things that make you feel truly alive?
